Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): clicking child content does not select cells using hostDirectives
Issues.Body: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When `GridCell` is applied to a reusable component through `hostDirectives`, clicking text inside a child `` moves focus to the cell but does not select it. Clicking the padding on the same cell selects it correctly. The reproduction shows a standard grid and a grid using `hostDirectives` side by side. Both use `enableSelection`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, and `multi`. The standard grid selects cells when clicking either their text or their padding. The reusable cell is defined as follows: ```ts @Component({ selector: 'composed-grid-cell', template: '', hostDirectives: [GridCell], }) class ComposedGridCell {} ``` Its content is ordinary markup, for example `Composed: Second`. This makes the clickable behavior depend on whether the user clicks the text or the surrounding padding. ### Reproduction StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts Wait for the preview to load. It uses Angular 22.2.4 and @angular/aria 22.2.6. **Visual indicators:** blue background = active/focused cell; green outline = selected cell. The dashed rectangle marks the child ``; the surrounding padding belongs directly to the cell host. Steps to reproduce with actual mouse clicks: 1. In the first grid, under **Direct ngGridCell**, click the text **Standard: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue and gets a green outline: it is active and selected. 2. In the second grid, under **hostDirectives**, click the text **Composed: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue but gets **no green outline**: focus moves, but selection does not change. 3. Click the padding of that same **Composed: Second** cell, outside its dashed rectangle. A green outline now appears: clicking the host directly selects it. Reload the preview to reset the demonstration. ### Expected Behavior With selection enabled, clicking non-interactive child content inside a cell should select the containing cell, just as clicking the cell host does. Using `GridCell` through `hostDirectives` should behave like direct `ngGridCell` usage. ### Actual Behavior | Usage / click target | Focus moves to second cell | Second cell selected | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct `ngGridCell`: child text | Yes | Yes | | `hostDirectives`: child text | Yes | **No** | | `hostDirectives`: cell padding | Yes | Yes | After clicking **Composed: Second** text, its host has `data-active="true"` but `aria-selected="false"`. Clicking its padding changes `aria-selected` to `"true"`. Possible cause: `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors with `closest('[ngGridCell]')`, but `GridCell` does not declare that marker as a static host attribute. The marker is present with direct template usage and absent with `hostDirectives`. This report is limited to the cell selection behavior demonstrated above. It does not claim that focus fails to move, or that `GridCellWidget` is affected. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.4 - Angular CLI / build: 22.2.4 - @angular/aria: 22.2.6 - @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 - TypeScript: 6.0.3 - Browser: Google Chrome - Operating system: macOS (Apple silicon) - Reproduction runs in StackBlitz. Regression status: unknown; an earlier working version has not been identified.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Enter on a menu item doesn't activate the element, so link items and (click) handlers are mouse-only
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Activating a menu item with the keyboard never reaches the item's element:

- `<a ngMenuItem href="...">` (or with `routerLink`) doesn't navigate on Enter.
- A `(click)` handler on `<button ngMenuItem>` doesn't run on Enter.

Clicking either item with the mouse works.

The menu's `KeyboardEventManager` calls `preventDefault()` on handled keys by default (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/behaviors/event-manager/keyboard-event-manager.ts#L34), which cancels the browser's own activation of a link or button. `MenuPattern.submit()` then closes the menu and emits `itemSelected`, but never activates the item itself (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L404-L421).

Navigation menus are a common use, and the WAI-ARIA APG navigation menubar example is built from `<a role="menuitem" href>` items that Enter follows. With the current behaviour, routing has to be rebuilt by hand in `itemSelected`, which also loses the href behaviours a link gives (open in new tab, etc.).

A possible fix: have `submit()` call `item.element.click()`. That's what native buttons and links do on Enter, and it makes keyboard and pointer activation run the same path.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section B; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu B" and press Enter. Focus is on "Go to #target" (`<a ngMenuItem href="#target">`).
2. Press Enter.
3. Reopen the menu, ArrowDown to "Button with (click)" and press Enter.
4. For comparison, click both items with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Step 2 navigates to #target, and step 3 runs the item's (click) handler ("(click) ran" appears in the log), the same as clicking them with the mouse.

### Actual Behavior

In both steps the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger, but the URL doesn't change and the (click) handler never runs. Mouse clicks navigate and run the handler.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

---
